question.problem: Consider the finite region bounded between the curves $y=x$ and $y={x}^{2}-2x.$ Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)={x}^{2}-2x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ x & ={x}^{2}-2x \\ {x}^{2}-3x & =0 \\ x(x-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=3.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=3.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14264628/assets/d34ebdf90ce2b2796e7ad6f06380c78edd43195ee71a59da4a9a3f877b8b9e1f.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)={x}^{2}-2x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=x.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}x([x]-[{x}^{2}-2x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}x(3x-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{3}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {({x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4})|}_{0}^{3} \\  & =2\pi [(27-\frac{81}{4})-0] \\  & =\frac{27\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
